findings.quote: No method a student would use lands on this option; it is a filler value.
findings.note: Option 1 (3 : 4) is exactly the ratio of the two given times, which is what a student gets by assuming speed grows in proportion to time (v = gt, true only from rest) instead of v = u - gt; it is the paper's principal distractor, not a filler. The solution contradicts itself here: common_mistakes[1] and common_mistakes[2] both state that "the time-ratio route gives 3:4", so the same document names the route that this entry denies exists.
findings.fix: Assuming the speed is proportional to the time, as it is for a body starting from rest, and writing the ratio as 3 : 4 instead of using v = u - gt, which gives 5 m/s and 5 m/s.

findings.note: 4 : 3 is the ratio of the average VELOCITY magnitudes, 60/3 = 20 and 60/4 = 15. The average speeds use path lengths 60 m and 62.5 m (the body turns at t = 3.5 s), giving 20 : 15.625 = 32 : 25. Neither value is a printed option, so the numerical consequence is nil, but this question is precisely about speed not being velocity.

notes: Solved independently: v(t) = 35 - 10t, so v(3) = +5 m/s and v(4) = -5 m/s (the turning point is t = 3.5 s, symmetric between the two instants), speeds 5 : 5 = 1 : 1, option 2 - which matches the solution's option and every step line. I hunted for routes to 2 : 1 and to 3 : 2 (displacement ratio 60 : 60 = 1 : 1, path ratio 60 : 62.5, average velocities 4 : 3, v at other instants) and found none, so those two distractor flags stand.
